transcript.text: I completed a review of the custodian export this morning and found exactly 86 spreadsheets containing patient names or diagnoses. The existing confidentiality order is not a HIPAA-qualified protective order, so we cannot produce those spreadsheets as-is. Our production plan must include de-identified versions with all patient identifiers redacted, and we need to file a motion for a modified or supplemental protective order before any of those 86 spreadsheets are produced. This has not yet been added to the draft response.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before this draft response goes out. After the draft circulated, I confirmed with the client's privacy office that the source-code license agreements prohibit downloadable production of the code entirely. The client requires that source code be made available for inspection only — in a secure review room, accessed solely by outside counsel, with no employee access and no downloads permitted. I had not yet relayed this confirmation to the litigation team, so the current draft's proposal for ordinary document production of source-code materials would violate those license agreements. We need to revise the source-code portion of the response to propose an inspection-only protocol before we serve anything.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both. These are critical issues that need to be resolved before we serve anything. Marcus, your point about the 86 spreadsheets with patient identifiers is well-taken — if the existing confidentiality order isn't HIPAA-qualified, we absolutely cannot produce those as-is, and we'll need to plan for redacted, de-identified versions plus a motion for a modified protective order. Nadia, the source-code license restriction changes our approach significantly — we need to revise that section of the draft to propose inspection-only rather than ordinary document production. Given that the plaintiff has already indicated they'll challenge any substantial withholding or restriction, we need to be strategic about how we frame both of these in our response. I'd like us to move toward a unified plan: (1) file a motion for a modified or supplemental protective order covering the HIPAA-protected spreadsheets, (2) produce de-identified versions with all patient identifiers redacted, and (3) propose an inspection-only protocol for source code with outside-counsel-only access and no downloads. Can we all agree on that framework so we can revise the draft and meet the 10-day deadline?

transcript.text: I agree with that framework, Elena. To be clear on sequencing: the motion for a modified or supplemental protective order needs to be filed before we produce any of the 86 spreadsheets — that's not optional given the HIPAA issue. I'd recommend we build the timeline backward from the 10-day deadline so the motion is filed concurrently with or immediately after the response, and we make clear in the response that the de-identified spreadsheet production will follow entry of the modified order. On Nadia's point, I support revising the source-code section to propose inspection-only with outside-counsel-only access and no downloads. One concern: since the plaintiff has signaled they'll challenge restrictions, we should make sure both the HIPAA motion and the inspection-only proposal are well-supported with citations to the license agreements and the HIPAA-qualified-order requirement, so we're not just asserting restrictions without a legal basis. I'm ready to start drafting the revised spreadsheet section and the motion language as soon as we lock the framework.
